findings.evidence: `grep -rn "LipschitzOnWith" TauCeti` returns hits only in `Winding/LipschitzBoundedIntegrand.lean`, `Winding/RealIntegral/OnCurve.lean:198,201`, `Complex/Conformal/NormalFamilies.lean` (for `f`, not a derivative) and three `Geometry/Lie` files — no lemma yields a Lipschitz `derivWithin`. Mathlib provides the pieces: `ContDiffOn.derivWithin` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Deriv.lean:64) and `ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/RCLike.lean:149).
findings.fix: Add the characteristic intro lemmas next to the definition: (i) `isLipschitzOnEachSideAt_of_contDiffOn : 0 < ε → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc (t - ε) (t + ε)) → IsLipschitzOnEachSideAt γ t`, via `ContDiffOn.derivWithin` + `ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith` on each half; and (ii) a restriction form taking `DifferentiableOn`/`LipschitzOnWith (derivWithin γ (Icc c t))`/`(Icc t d)` on arbitrary one-sided pieces `c < t < d`.
findings.issue: `IsLipschitzOnEachSideAt` is a new public predicate that gates all three public results, but it has no introduction lemma and no restriction/shrinking lemma. Nothing in the repo produces `LipschitzOnWith K (derivWithin γ (Icc ...))`, so a caller must build the 8-binder existential from scratch — including the natural `C²` case the roadmap's next Layer 1 target (the `½·k·|Λ̇|` crossing value, stated for `C²` crossings) will need, and the case where the caller already has `C^{1,1}` on wider one-sided pieces `[c, t]`, `[t, d]` and must shrink to the `εL`/`εR` form.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn "realWindingIntegrand" TauCeti`: every other statement (`CrossingValue/Basic.lean:114`, `CrossingValue/Curvature.lean:154,180`, `BoundedIntegrand.lean:131`, `LipschitzBoundedIntegrand.lean`, `OnCurve.lean:486`) uses `realWindingIntegrand`; `Basic.lean:76-79` is the only unfolded one. `grep -rn "windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed" TauCeti` shows no callers.
findings.fix: Restate `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed`'s conclusion as `∫ t in a..b, realWindingIntegrand (γ t - w) (deriv γ t)` (the proof already goes through `realWindingIntegrand_eq_div`/`realWindingIntegrand_def`); it has no in-repo callers, so nothing else changes.
findings.issue: The canonical API now states HW Prop 2.3 two ways: the new `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed_interior_crossings` concludes with `∫ realWindingIntegrand (γ t - s) (deriv γ t)`, while its sibling `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed` in the same directory concludes with the unfolded `((γ t - w).re * (deriv γ t).im - ...) / Complex.normSq (γ t - w)`. A consumer cannot move between the off-curve and on-curve forms by `rw`, and the named abstraction is bypassed in exactly the one place it is the subject.

findings.evidence: OnCurve.lean:409-414 and 438-443 are byte-identical docstrings on two different declarations; `isBounded_intervalIntegrable_cauchyPV_of_interior_crossings` is declared `private theorem` at line 217, and `_uIcc` is `private theorem` at line 415.
findings.fix: Give the `_uIcc` bundle its own docstring describing the three facts it returns; in the two public docstrings, drop the reference to the private name (state the content, or point at `windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed_interior_crossings`).
findings.issue: `isBounded_intervalIntegrable_cauchyPV_of_interior_crossings_uIcc` carries a verbatim copy of the boundedness projection's docstring — it calls itself "Projection of `isBounded_intervalIntegrable_cauchyPV_of_interior_crossings`" and the "boundedness half", though it is the orientation-generic bundle of all three facts and is what the projections project from. Separately, the two public theorems at lines 444 and 457 document themselves as projections of `isBounded_intervalIntegrable_cauchyPV_of_interior_crossings`, a `private` declaration that never appears in generated docs (and is not the theorem they actually project from — that is the `_uIcc` form).

summary: The new public hypothesis-predicate `IsLipschitzOnEachSideAt` ships with no introduction or restriction API, so no consumer can discharge `hγ_lip` for a concrete curve; additionally the two sibling HW Prop 2.3 theorems now state the same integral in two different spellings, and several docstrings on the new public surface point at a private declaration or are verbatim copies of the wrong one.
